content_sections.heading: About the NATCOM Cell IPMU
content_sections.text: The NATCOM Cell is a unit of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, located at Indira Paryavaran Bhawan, New Delhi. Its Integrated Project Management Unit runs the GEF-UNDP-MoEFCC Projects for the National Communications and Biennial Transparency Reports to UNFCCC. The notice is signed by the National Project Director, NATCOM Cell, and is dated 18 November 2026.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Experience: more than 3 years to up to 5 years, in relevant experience (post qualification) in climate change and related fields. Experience includes up to 3 years for PhD holders, provided no experience is counted during those 3 years. The experience must be in the relevant field of specialized work with good computer skills. Desirable: Previous experience in project coordination or relevant internships is a plus. General understanding of climate change issues and sustainability. Familiarity with climate change adaptation and mitigation measures. Age: upper age limit 32 years. The notice states that the maximum age limit is as specified in the Terms of Reference. It prints no cut-off date for counting age and no age relaxation. Consultants Grade-I, Consultants Grade-II, Young Professionals and Consultant-B already working with the Ministry can apply for a higher Consultancy position in MoEFCC, competing with external candidates, provided they meet the eligibility criteria for the higher position that is advertised. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility details.

rows.essential_qualification: Master's degree from a recognized institution in Environmental studies, Climate Change, Development studies or related fields, OR B.Tech. in Environmental Engineering or related fields.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The consolidated remuneration is INR 70,000/- per month and is paid through UNDP on the recommendation of the National Project Director. It is inclusive of all applicable taxes and no other facility or allowance is allowed. For retired Government employees engaged as consultants, remuneration and transport allowance are governed by the D/o Expenditure OM dated 09.12.2020, as amended from time to time or as prescribed by the Central Government. The engagement is initially for two years. Extension is based on performance appraisal and mutual willingness, up to 2028 or project duration, whichever is earlier, on a case-to-case basis. Annual increment is between 0% to 8% of the remuneration, depending on the quality of performance, decided by the National Project Director case to case. Paid leave is 1.5 days for each completed month of service, accruing on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Un-availed leave cannot be carried forward to the next tenure of 1 year. No remuneration is drawn for absence beyond 18 days in a year, calculated pro-rata. Female Consultants are eligible for maternity leave under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended from time to time.

content_sections.heading: MoEFCC Young Professional (Technical) Job Description
content_sections.text: Assist the NPD and technical staff of PMU in coordinating project activities, ensuring adherence to project timelines, and tracking progress. Coordinate with partner institutions for collation of data and information related to project activities. Assist in organizing and maintaining project related data. Maintain project documentation, including meeting minutes, progress reports, and project related studies outputs. Support the preparation of project reports, presentations. Assist in coordinating stakeholder consultations and feedback mechanisms. Contribute to knowledge sharing efforts, extraction and dissemination of relevant climate change information and best practices. The Consultant reports to the National Project Director and works under the day-to-day supervision of the NPD and the Scientists in the NATCOM Division. Performance is evaluated annually.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for MoEFCC Young Professional (Technical)
content_sections.text: Fill the application online via the Microsoft Form "Young Professional (Technical) – Fill out form". Prepare the CV in the format given at Annexure 1 of the notice, which asks for personal details, educational qualifications, employment details, courses, publications, languages known, contact details and additional information in support of suitability. Attach self-attested copies of the documents named below; total attachments must not exceed 10 MB. Sign the undertaking at the end of the Annexure 1 template. Send the CV by email to [email protected] so that the application is received by 17 December 2026. Documents named in the notice: PhD Certificate (if any) Masters' Degree Certificate (if applicable) Bachelor's Degree Certificate (if applicable) Experience Certificates Age proof

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: All applications received are scrutinized and shortlisted by UNDP in association with the NATCOM Cell. A list of suitable candidates in the ratio 1:5 goes to the Selection Committee approved by the Secretary. The Selection Committee finalizes the candidates based on the interview of all the candidates and gives the list of shortlisted candidates to the Ministry. A waitlist of qualified candidates, nearly 2 times the number of vacancies, is kept in panel for three years and is considered in cases of transfer, resignation, death and similar. The notice does not mention an interview date or venue.

faq.question: Q1. How many Young Professional (Technical) posts are advertised by MoEFCC?
faq.answer: One (01) Young Professional (Technical) position is advertised in the IPMU of the NATCOM Cell, MoEFCC, New Delhi, on a contractual basis.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: The last date for receipt of applications is 17 December 2026. Applications received after the due date will not be considered.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is required?
faq.answer: A Master's degree from a recognized institution in Environmental studies, Climate Change, Development studies or related fields, or a B.Tech. in Environmental Engineering or related fields. Relevant experience of more than 3 years to up to 5 years is also required.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: The upper age limit is 32 years. The notice prints no age relaxation and no cut-off date for age.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary?
faq.answer: The consolidated remuneration is INR 70,000/- per month, inclusive of all applicable taxes, with no other facility or allowance, and paid through UNDP.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply?
faq.answer: Fill the Microsoft Form "Young Professional (Technical) – Fill out form" and email the CV in the Annexure 1 format to [email protected].

faq.question: Q7. How are candidates selected?
faq.answer: UNDP and the NATCOM Cell shortlist applications and send a list in the ratio 1:5 to the Selection Committee, which finalizes candidates based on the interview.

faq.question: Q8. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. It is a contractual, temporary (non-official) engagement, initially for two years, with extension up to 2028 or project duration, whichever is earlier.

faq.question: Q9. Will TA/DA be paid for attending the interview?
faq.answer: No. The notice says no TA/DA is payable by the Ministry to attend the interview.

faq.question: Q10. Can existing MoEFCC consultants apply?
faq.answer: Yes. Consultants Grade-I, Consultants Grade-II, Young Professionals and Consultant-B already working with the Ministry can apply for a higher Consultancy position, provided they meet its eligibility criteria.
